newsitem.title: UK: Reuters jumps on special dividend news.
newsitem.headline: Reuters jumps on special dividend news.

text.p: Shares in Reuters Holdings Plc jumped on Wednesday after the company said it proposed to return 613 million stg of cash to shareholders over three years through a bonus issue of a new class of special dividend shares, traders said.
Shares in the international news and information organisation jumped 29p to 779p after reversing a 5p decline immediately prior to the buyback news.
Trading volumes also surged and by 1130 GMT had passed seven million.
"The sum is a bit larger than people had been looking for, but then it is over three years," said SG Strauss Turnbull analyst Jason Crisp.
Under the proposal, with a share capital consolidation, shareholders will receive 19 ordinary shares and one special dividend share for every 20 shares held on October 8.
Each special dividend share will pay net dividends totalling 750p over the period against an average of the ordinary share price of 752p for the week to 9 September 1996, Reuters said.
The consolidation will result in a five percent reduction in the number of ordinary shares in issue, Reuters said.
"The company considers the proposal to be the best way of enabling shareholders to receive more cash, more efficiently, at a faster rate and on an equal basis," it said.
